items.fromString:
h3. Why

Checkout today is a saga of queue messages between shop-api and shop-worker: reserve stock, authorize the card, create the order, send the confirmation. Each step retries on its own, and when one step gives up the compensations are best effort. Support sees about 40 orders a week with a captured payment and no order, or an order with released stock.

A durable workflow engine keeps the state of each checkout, retries each activity with its own policy, and runs the compensations in order when a step fails for good.

h3. Scope

* A pure workflow function {{checkoutWorkflow(cart)}} in {{@acme/shop-shared}}, with no I/O of its own.
* Activities in shop-worker: {{reserveStock}}, {{authorizePayment}}, {{createOrder}}, {{sendConfirmation}} and their compensations.
* A gate in {{POST /checkout}} that sends a share of carts to the new path, by the {{checkout_v2_percent}} flag.
* Replay tests that run recorded histories against every new build of the workflow.

h3. Out of scope

* Moving cart storage to PostgreSQL (SHOP-3463).
* Changes to the payments provider or its webhooks.

issuetype.name: Story

content.text: With the flag at 100% in staging, 10 000 synthetic checkouts end with no captured payment that lacks an order.
Killing any activity worker mid-checkout resumes the checkout from its last completed step.
A payment declined after the stock was reserved releases the stock within 5 seconds.
Checkout P90 on the new path is no worse than on the saga path.
Replay tests run in CI on every pull request that touches the workflow.
